data.narrative:
Marvel Fusion, a Series B-stage nuclear energy company founded by Moritz von der Linden, is evaluated against a comp universe of 11 peers: three public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and eight private firms including Valar Atomics, Helion, Oklo, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy. The target has raised $400M+ to date.

The Stage-Progression method is applicable and yields a $760M implied valuation, derived by applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B progression to the $400M total raised proxy. The Peer-Median approach is not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow nuclear energy set; only one same-stage peer was identified, falling short of the three-point minimum required for robust cross-sectional inference. Expanding to all six nuclear energy peers would introduce sector-level noise unrelated to Marvel Fusion's specific position.

The triangulation analysis, constrained to one applicable method, supports a valuation range of $646M (low) to $874M (high), with a median of $760M. The binding uncertainty is the sparse peer dataset in early-stage nuclear energy; only the stage-progression methodology provides quantitative grounding. Validation of this range would benefit from additional Series B nuclear comparables or revenue-multiple anchoring if operating metrics become available. The $400M+ raised baseline itself carries execution risk regarding deployment and capital efficiency.
